The immediate trigger for writing this was mechanical, not curatorial: test_db_integrity's L04 fails when sessions/LATEST-RESEARCH names a session with zero slug-linked Tier 1-2 sources, because the blocking citation_mining_session gate then examines nothing and passes. Batch 07 admitted only Tier 3, so the pointer had to name batch 06, and batch 06 had no record to name. Logged so nobody later reads this reconstruction as routine housekeeping.

bias_direction: Writing another session's record invites two opposite distortions and the stronger pull here was the flattering one: batch 06 produced the project's first determination, and a reconstruction written by the session that just cleared its blocker has every incentive to describe it as clean. The counter-pressure I applied was to restrict the file to figures I could re-derive by query and to state the two things it cannot supply. The opposite distortion -- writing batch 06 down to make batch 07's provisional result look comparatively rigorous -- was available too, and the REF-00784 demotion paragraph is where it would have shown; that paragraph states the demotion does not affect the determination, because it does not.
independent_reviewer_counterclaim: A reviewer would reasonably object that a record reconstructed by a later session should not exist at all, because it makes an un-closed session look closed, and that the honest state was the visible gap. The strongest version: the pointer problem could have been solved by demoting citation_mining_session to advisory, which L04's own message offers as the alternative remedy, leaving batch 06 conspicuously unrecorded until its own author closed it. I chose the record because demoting a blocking gate is a larger and more permanent act than writing a labelled reconstruction, and because the gap was costing a real audit every day it stood -- but the objection is sound and the choice was mine, not forced.
